title: Introduce presubmit lighthouse and slim toolchain bootstrap
author: Sofia Patel
release_notes: Adds a presubmit scoring/early-gating component (presubmit-lighthouse) and shrinks toolchain bootstrap images for faster dev CI start-up. Improves presubmit feedback latency by reducing init IO and trimming test matrix for quick-feedback lanes.
description: Context: our presubmit latency budget is dominated by toolchain init (image pulls, venv setup) and long-running lint/test shards on low-risk changes. This PR introduces 'presubmit-lighthouse', a lightweight presubmit prober that estimates CI cost and quality impact and applies stage-aware gates. It also ships a slim toolchain bootstrap path (micro-images + precompiled wheels) and a presubmit-pruner that reduces the footprint of tests and devdeps for the fast-feedback lane. Motivation: reduce flakiness/queue time, improve first-response time for engineers, and lower CI egress/storage costs. What changed: - presubmit-lighthouse service (Go): scoring API, rule registry, and a small RBAC-protected admin flag to opt into stricter gating. - presubmit-pruner (Python): change-aware test selection heuristics and devdep trim list. - toolchain-slim images: split the monolith image into micro-images (runtime-base, build-essentials, python-wheels) and a lazy-join bootstrap script that composes them when needed. - CI workflows: new fastpath-presubmit lane that uses the slim toolchain and pruner plus a staged lint shard. - Console + telemetry: added presubmit.score and presubmit.estimated_cost metrics, surfaced in the pipeline trace. Rollout plan: deploy presubmit-lighthouse behind a feature flag; enable scoring-only mode for 48h, then auto-block on score>=0.8 for opt-in orgs; monitor presubmit.score and build.queue_time for regressions. Testing: unit tests for Go service and Python pruner; end-to-end smoke runs in staging; dogfooding across three active teams for 7 days. Risks and mitigations: - false positives (over-pruning tests): pruner has a safe-mode that falls back to full matrix if flakiness exceeds threshold. - initial image cache misses: images are staged in the edge registry with a warmup job. - scoring model regressions: score history retained and alerts trigger when pass-rate drops >2% in fastpath. Related: ENG-3421, ENG-3470. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked - [x] unit tests - [x] e2e smoke - [x] telemetry events - [x] rollout playbook added to ops-runbook

review_comments: Marcus Lee: Can we make the score thresholds configurable per-ORG? I want customer teams to opt-in before block mode. [response] Sofia: Yes — added an org-level config and admin flag. See internal/lighthouse/config.go.

Amina Yusuf: Pruner seems aggressive on fixtures/serialization tests — how do we avoid flaking? [response] Sofia: Added safe-mode: if pruner causes failure rate >1% in canary, we auto-disable for that repo and ship full matrix. Added per-test weight override file.

Kevin O'Rourke: CI image assembly looks fine, but ensure the lazy-join script respects proxy settings. [response] Sofia: addressed; added proxy detection and a network timeout guard in infra/images/toolchain/bootstrap.sh
QA Bot: integration-smoke failed on first run (timeout pulling image) and passed on rerun. Sofia: warmup job added to registry; flake noted in staging and cleared.

notes_for_reviewers: Focus reviews on: rule coverage in internal/lighthouse/rules.go, the safe-mode thresholds in pruner.py, and bootstrap script's network/proxy handling. Performance note: initial runs reduce avg init time from ~22s to ~6s for fastpath (staging sample).
maintenance_estimate: Monitor for 2 weeks after enabling score-block; plan 2 follow-up PRs: (1) housekeeper to trim stale rule entries, (2) expand pruner weights by language.
ci_flakiness_observation: Observed one transient timeout on initial image pull in GH runners; mitigated by registry warmup job and retry with backoff in bootstrap script. No further flakiness in subsequent runs.
